text:
cheng.li: kicking off tonight's kernel microbench sweep. added variance detector + seqpath grouping. uploading to s3 at s3://redwood-ci/kbench/3588888000/ . trying to catch seqlen-sensitive picks that flip between ampere/h100.

maria.d: awesome. is this the run that exercises KV cache hot vs cold? need those diffs for the batching heuristic change.

cheng.li: yeah - there are three modes: prefill-only (cold kv), decode-only (warm kv), and mixed. Also we added seqlen buckets: 32, 128, 512, 2048.

samir: nice. what are the gating rules? last time we had a false positive due to variance.

cheng.li: new rule: require 3 independent hosts, median latency improvement >= 2% and p-value < 0.01 (wilcoxon) OR improvement in 95th percentile > 3%. also flag if stddev across hosts > 8% -> mark flaky.

oliver: can we see command to reproduce locally?

cheng.li: ```
krnlbench run --arch ampere,h100 --seq-buckets 32,128,512,2048 --modes prefill,decode,mixed --runs 50 --out results.json --run-id 3588888000
```

maria.d: pinging infra to increase concurrency for next night, tests were queueing last sweep.

runtime-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-ci/kbench/3588888000/results.json :white_check_mark:

samir: quick look — seqlen 2048 picks are flipping on ampere vs h100, seems related to KV prefetch path. log excerpt:
```
[ampere][seq=2048][prefill] kernel=cuda_conv_v2 latency=12.4ms
[h100][seq=2048][prefill] kernel=cuda_conv_v3 latency=10.1ms
[ampere][seq=2048][decode] kernel=cuda_kvpath latency=9.8ms
```

oliver: hmm that decode path on ampere is better in decode but prefill worse. maybe dispatch heuristic needs split by mode not just seqlen.

cheng.li: agreed. proposing we add 'mode-aware' kernel selection: pick kernel per (arch, seq_bucket, mode) tuple. it'll increase autotune state but reduce wrong picks.

maria.d: sounds good. what's the perf CI change? will candidate kernels get auto-rejected?

cheng.li: perf CI will now run the variance detector and gating. candidates failing gating will be annotated and not promoted. we keep artifacts for manual triage.

samir: please add a step to run the deterministic microprobe (single-thread, cpu isolation) for any flaky candidates so we can reduce noise.

cheng.li: added to backlog and the harness - see PR #4523 for wiring. small snippet of new detector config:
```
variance_detector:
  hosts_required: 3
  runs_per_host: 50
  seq_buckets: [32,128,512,2048]
  mode_sensitive: true
  flaky_stddev_threshold: 0.08
  pvalue_threshold: 0.01
```

oliver: one more ask - can we publish a brief triage playbook for when kernel flips happen? so oncall knows steps.

cheng.li: yes, drafting a playbook in eng-runtime/wiki. top-level steps: reproduce, run deterministic microprobe, check KV stats, compare perf traces, tag candidate flaky/ok.

runtime-bot: nightly sweep summary: 42 candidates tested, 7 gated (3 flaky, 4 regressions), 2 flagged for manual triage. dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/kbench/3588888000

samir: :thumbsup: great. I'll take the 2 triage items tomorrow.

maria.d: thanks team. can we get a short email to PLs summarizing gating thresholds change?

cheng.li: will send morning. including notable regression: ampere prefill for seq=512 saw +6.2% 95p latency due to kernel fallback.

oliver: adding a note to the rollout playbook to prefer mode-aware picks for canary.

runtime-bot: CI artifact link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-ci/kbench/3588888000/results.json?region=us-west-2
